messages:
Olivia: hey @ravi @sam — marketing preparing the launch post and we need a short audit of the benchmark aggregation logic before publishing. can eng/runtime validate the P50/P95 aggregation across shards and confirm what warmup strategy you used?

Sam: can you list the exact payloads and model variants you used in the topline figures? we need reproducible steps.

Olivia: absolutely. sample payloads below (used 3 seq-length buckets: short/med/long). also ran on both fp16 and int8 quantized builds.

```
# short
{"input": "Summarize: The product helps devs ship LLM features.", "tokens": 32}
# med
{"input": "Explain how Redwood reduces inference cost and latency for production apps.", "tokens": 128}
# long
{"input": "Long prompt... (~1024 tokens) - simulated multi-turn context", "tokens": 1024}
```

Olivia: run settings: batch_size=8, concurrency=16, 30s steady-state after warmup, 5 repeats per config. model tags used: rdx-13b-v1, rdx-13b-v1-quant-int8. exported results were aggregated by taking per-shard token throughput then computing median across shards for P50/P95.

Ravi: thanks — couple quick clarifications: 1) when you say "per-shard median" do you mean you computed P50 per shard then took the median of those P50s? or you merged raw request latencies across shards then computed P50/P95 on the pooled set? those two differ.

Olivia: great question — marketing doc currently says "median of shard-level P50s" because we wanted to avoid outlier noise from a single noisy host. open to changing if eng recommends pooled stats.

Ravi: eng-runtime prefers pooled latencies for accuracy, but we can produce both. pooled gives true user-level percentiles; shard-median is more stable for slides. we'll run both and flag differences. also for quantized runs we need 5+ repeats and to capture p99 to spot tails.

Jordan: please include cold-starts (first 10 requests) and streaming fallback cases (simulate 1 token/sec streaming to catch buffer behavior).

Mia: for the PR deck we need per-token CPU/GPU utilization and memory headroom snapshots. ideally CSVs so marketing can make charts.

Olivia: noted. also add the exact command used to run the bench in the thread so we can reproduce.

Ravi: example run command we'll use: `./bench_runner --model rdx-13b-v1 --quant int8 --batch 8 --concurrency 16 --steady 30 --repeat 5 --output-dir /tmp/bench-2111` — we'll attach run metadata (run_id, seed, node list).

bench-bot: queued benchmark job 2111-rt-045 for rdx-13b-v1 (quant=int8).

Ravi: queued. ETA ~24h for full sweep (both fp16 + int8, 5 repeats, pooled + shard-median outputs). we'll also produce per-token traces and a small note about observed variance.

Olivia: amazing — can you post the run_id(s) and a short summary when done? marketing will draft the blog based on the pooled stats but will call out method (and include shard-median as appendix). :+1:

Sam: minor ask — tag any runs that had GPU mem spikes >90% so we don't include inflated latency from OOM-induced retries.

Ravi: will do. we'll also attach raw logs and a tiny parsing script to regenerate the CSVs.

Jordan: if the int8 runs are noisier, please include quantized quality delta (sampled outputs) so product can sign off on messaging.

Olivia: yes — add a small qualitative sample set (10 prompts) comparing outputs across variants. marketing legal will review claims.

Ravi: noted. I'll update this thread with run_id and summary once the sweep finishes.

Olivia: thanks team — much appreciated :pray:
